name: Griffin Mission One

surface_window.note: The landing date is not published.

outcome_note: Griffin-1 plans to launch in late 2026; five NASA payloads will be mounted on the Astrolab FLIP rover (NASA, Aug 2026). VIPER, originally on this task order, moved to Blue Origin under CS-7.

payloads.name: Laser Retroreflector Array
payloads.purpose: Passive retroreflectors serving as a precise location marker.

sources.title: NASA Provides Updates on Moon Base Cargo Landers, Tech Demonstrations (Aug 04, 2026)
Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) Deliveries (page updated May 06, 2026)
Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Mons Mouton
Launch Library 2 launch record: Falcon Heavy | Griffin Mission One

notes: NASA's TO20A page names one payload (LRA); NASA's Aug 2026 update says five NASA payloads on the FLIP rover. Only the named one is listed.
The deliveries overview still says 'Astrobotic's Griffin lander ... in 2025'; the Aug 2026 pages name Voyager Technologies. The newer pages are used.
The target coordinate is the IAU centre of Mons Mouton, not a published landing point.

Launch Library 2 lists Griffin Mission One on Falcon Heavy from LC-39A, no earlier than November 2026, with its status 'to be determined' (a placeholder date). NASA's August 2026 update says 'late 2026'; that is the date used.

site.name: Mons Mouton (feature centre)
site.source_note: The IAU centre of Mons Mouton, used because no landing point is published. It is not a landing point, and numbers here describe the centre of the named feature. Height and slope sampled from the 80 m LOLA model at the nearest post.

notes: Mission facts are compiled by hand from NASA pages, LROC images and the IAU Gazetteer; every record carries its sources, last read 2026-09-27.
1 of 1 missions have fields no source confirms; they are listed as unconfirmed, never filled in.
Numbers are Sun and Earth geometry at the target over the mission's surface window, not what any lander measured.
Where no landing point is published, the target is the IAU centre of the named feature, which is not a landing point.
